steps.step: Prepare a suspension of 3.0 g poly-ß-hydroxybutyric acid (PHB) in 100 ml distilled water, stir over night and sonicate until a white homogenous suspension is obtained. Autoclave for 5 minutes at 121°C. Prepare double layer agar plates. First layer: medium 457 with 16.0 g agar per l.
Second layer: medium 457 with agar, supplemented with 6.6 ml sterile PHB-suspension per 100 ml.
Adjust pH to 6.9.

Add the top layer solution in 5 to 6 times the volume of the bottom layer to the culture vessels containing the bottom layer (e.g., 25 to 30 ml in 60 ml glass vials with 5 ml of the bottom layer).
Then, cap the culture vessels with silicone rubber stoppers, and replace the gas phase with a N2-CO2 (4:1, v/v) gas mixture.

Comment: The medium can be stored in culture vessels for a certain time by capping with butyl rubber stoppers, instead of silicon rubber stoppers and keeping anoxic in the vessels. Silicone rubber stopper is O2 permeable and creates a mircoaerophilic condition in the culture vessels.

Prewarm distilled water at 50C in a beaker with a stir bar. While rapidly starring the water, add FeSO4 x 7H2O, followed immediately by Na2S x 9H2O. A thick black precipitate will form instantly. Stir continuously for 2 to 3 min. Remove the mixture to a narrow-mouthed glass bottle (500 ml) that can be tightly stopped. The bottle is filled to the top with distilled water and capped. Allow to settle for several hours, decant and replace the overlaying water. Repeat this procedure at least five times to wash the FeS precipitate. Check pH to be close to neutral. To stock the FeS solution, fill the bottle with distilled water and cap. Remove the overlaying water when prepare the bottom layer.
